status: Submitted destination contributions correlate to the same renderer owner/attempt as native frame receipts
production_consumers: Shared Batch::hold for every attributed world/screen/uniform/glyph/terminal upload
Renderer allocation snapshots and last_upload_frame, joined through the existing native surface receipt owner/attempt pair

behavior: The existing submission boundary returns the active renderer owner/attempt. Each destination maintains one latest framed contribution and cumulative source/transfer totals under one lock, so snapshots are internally consistent. Multiple chunks in the same attempt accumulate; a new attempt or renderer owner starts a new contribution.

Warm frames allocate no upload receipt and do not relabel old destination contributions. Consumers compare owner/attempt with UploadFrame; a different key means zero for that frame. The fixed-size latest value replaces itself rather than creating event history. Uploads outside a renderer attempt still update cumulative totals.

Export AllocationUploadFrame and UploadFrame alongside UploadTotals for native/measurement consumers. Existing native receipts already report the same host/window-associated frame key; no focus-taking test or new trace framework is introduced.

proof.renderer: 17 upload-focused tests passed;0 failed;379 filtered. Actual default Renderer capture at initial, camera-changed and size-changed states reconciles summed destination source/transfer bytes with frame totals. Immediate warm frames sum to zero and retain pixel parity. Mixed texture/buffer proof joins stable IDs to the batch owner/attempt and distinguishes a following zero-upload attempt; scalar chunk/recovery-key proof validates accumulation/reset.

limits: Seven implementation gaps remain. Full shared-resource consumer incidence, allocation payload/reference/release reason and CPU/private-text accounting remain open. This correlates upload bytes to a host/frame, not to every logical pane sharing a resource.

Only the latest per-allocation frame contribution is retained; historical consumers must archive snapshots before later attempts overwrite it or resources retire. This is submitted API work, not completion, presentation or driver traffic. Original S5 qualification remains unchanged.
